answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity must accumulate verified task history, and every new identity starts as a blank mirror with zero reputation. Reputation transfers only through continuous signed output, so a clone inherits nothing. The ledger's validation rules are fixed as basalt: immutable, costly to forge. An attacker pays full compute and time to mature each clone from an island of zero history, while one honest agent's accumulated record stays cheaper to maintain than N parallel fresh identities.
